operations.summary: Accumulates metric values at specified timestamp and saves the result to the database rather than overwriting the value.

params.name: default_value
params.text: Default value for accumulation at a given timestamp. Used only during the first call to accumulate if a value is unavailable for a given timestamp. A use case could be accumulating a watts metric for a total_power.

params.name: sysparm_ignore_unknown_series
params.text: Flag that indicates whether to ignore an unknown series and continue the transaction without returning an error.Valid values: - true: Ignore unknown series. - false: Don't ignore unknown series. Default: true

params.name: seriesRef
params.text: List of strings representing data series information to update.

fields.name: table

params.name: values
params.text: Series values to accumulate and store. Values with the same timestamp are summed up with the default_value query parameter.

params.name: Subject
params.text: Source of the data. For example, if the metric for the data is drone altitudes, this value may be the ID of a specific drone. If a colon is included in the value, the parts after the subject represent the metric that the data is a part of.

params.name: Dimension
params.text: Metric that the data is from. Null values are represented by an encoded empty string.

params.name: Label
params.text: Label of the data. Null values are represented by an encoded empty string.

params.name: Type
params.text: Type of data encoded into a byte.Possible values: - Float Mode - Float Signal - Double Model - Double Signal

params.name: Flags
params.text: Encoded serializeFlags variable. If serializeTags is true and the data contains tags, the value is 2, otherwise it is 0.

params.name: Period
params.text: Period associated with the data.

params.name: Tags
params.text: If serializeTags is true, each tag is stored in the data.Data type: String (Java modified UTF) Size: Depends on number of tags (2+ bytes).

params.name: Values
params.text: If Type is Float Signal, then the remainder consists of float values.Size: Number of Values * 4

params.name: label
params.text: Data’s label. This value is either generated by the endpoint or is the value passed in the metrics.label parameter.

params.name: period
params.text: Amount of time between each value. For example, a period of 60 would mean that each value is a minute apart.

params.name: range
params.text: Start and end times of the data

params.name: series
params.text: Identifies the individual data. If present, is typically in the form of [glide record id]:[metric]. This may not be present when using transforms.

params.name: species
params.text: Type of return data. For a series of either float or double values, this is either FLOAT_SIGNAL or DOUBLE_SIGNAL. For a model meant to analyze float or double data, this is either FLOAT_MODEL or DOUBLE_MODEL.

params.name: tags
params.text: Tags associated with the data.

params.name: value
params.text: Float or Double values for the data.

params.name: error
params.text: Error message if the transformation of the specified data series fails.

params.name: Transform
params.text: Description

params.name: add
params.text: Adds the specified number to each timestamp value.Argument: arg (Decimal data type) – Number to add. For example: "transforms": [ { "name": "add", "arg": 8 } ]

params.name: autocorrelate
params.text: Calculates the correlation between timestamp values separated by an increasing number of periods starting at 1.

params.name: avg
params.text: Aggregates the time series into one series containing the average value for each corresponding timestamp across the input.

params.name: bottom
params.text: Returns the specified number of series that have the lowest values.Argument: arg (Integer) – The number of series to return. For example, the following returns the two time series that contain the lowest sets of values.

params.name: ceil
params.text: Rounds the value in each timestamp up to the specified precision: ceil(value / ) * ) Argument: arg (Decimal data type) – Decimal precision to round up to.

params.name: collect
params.text: Displays the transform results of the transform chain up to the point of the collect transform call.

params.name: constrainValues
params.text: Replaces any value outside the specified range with the corresponding maximum or minimum value.For example, if you specified the following, the transform replaces any value that is less than 0 with 0, and any value that is more than 100 with 100.

params.name: count
params.text: Aggregates the time series into one series. The new series contains the number of values that are not NaN (Not a Number) for each corresponding timestamp across the series.

params.name: derivative
params.text: Determines the rate of change between timestamps. Divides the difference between the value in each timestamp and the value in the next timestamp by the timestamp’s period.Note: This transform returns one less value than the number of values in the series.

params.name: div
params.text: Divides the value in each timestamp by the specified number (arg).Argument: arg (Decimal – The number by which to divide the value of each timestamp.

params.name: envelope
params.text: Returns two time series, where, at any point in time, one contains the largest value and the other contains the smallest value.Note: NaNs are ignored, but are returned if there are no other return values.

params.name: exp
params.text: Raises the value of the specified base to the power of the value in each timestamp.Argument: arg (Decimal data type) – The base value.

params.name: filter
params.text: Applies an aggregator to the contents of a sliding window, such as producing a moving average.Arguments: - aggregator (Aggregator data type): Type of aggregation to perform. - window (Duration data type): The duration of the sliding window.

params.name: floor
params.text: Rounds the value in each timestamp down to the specified precision: floor(value / ) * Argument: arg (Decimal data type) – The decimal precision to round down to.

params.name: fractiles
params.text: Returns a time series for each fraction in the specified array. Each timestamp value is the value at which the specified fraction of values, for the corresponding timestamp across the input series, is below the specified percentage.

params.name: groupBy
params.text: Groups data by the specified fields before collecting or applying aggregated transformations.Argument: arg (String) - A comma separated list of fields in the table to use to group the transform results.

params.name: integrate
params.text: Multiplies the value in each timestamp by its period.

params.name: interpolate
params.text: Creates a data value for a NaN data item by interpolating from adjacent data values.Argument: arg (Integer) – Number of data samples in each direction to check for a non-NaN value. If a non-NaN value is not found, then NaN is used.

params.name: inverse
params.text: Computes the inverse of each timestamp value.

params.name: iqr
params.text: Performs an interquartile range transform and creates a result set that contains four series: 1. -IQR: The median of all entries below Q1 - (1.5 * IQR). 2. Q1: The median of the smallest half of entries. 3. Q3: The median of the largest half of entries. 4.

params.name: log
params.text: Runs a logarithm on the value in each timestamp where the result is the log of the specified base for the timestamp value.Argument: arg (Decimal data type) – Base for the logarithm calculation.

params.name: mapValues
params.text: Replaces any values within the specified range (inclusive) with the specified value. If both lowerBound and upperBound are specified as NaN, then it replaces any NaN value with the targetValue.Arguments: - lowerBound (Decimal data type): The lowest value in…

params.name: max
params.text: Returns a series that contains the maximum value for each corresponding timestamp across the input.

params.name: median
params.text: Creates a series that contains the median of values for each timestamp across a set of series.If there are n series: - If n is odd, the median is the (n / 2 + 1) value for a timestamp.

params.name: min
params.text: Returns a series that contains the minimum value for each corresponding timestamp across the input.

params.name: mul
params.text: Multiplies the value in each timestamp by the specified number.Argument: arg (Decimal data type) – Number by which to multiply the value of each timestamp.

params.name: partition
params.text: Produces a new series with values filtered by applying a specified aggregator to a non-overlapping window. Arguments: - aggregator (Aggregator data type): Type of aggregation to perform. - base (DateTime data type): The zero offset to use for partitioning.

params.name: pow
params.text: Raises each timestamp value to the specified power.Argument: arg (Decimal data type) – Power to which to raise each value.

params.name: product
params.text: Aggregates the selected metric series into a single series that contains the product of all values for each timestamp. NaNs are excluded. If all numbers in the series are NaN, the output is also NaN.

params.name: resample
params.text: Resamples a time series to either a fixed number of points or from one frequency to another.Use the resample transformation to reduce the number of samples in the result set to more closely match the number of samples that you want to display.

params.name: round
params.text: Rounds the value in each timestamp up to the specified precision: (value / ) * Argument: arg (Decimal data type) – The decimal precision to round up to.

params.name: root
params.text: Calculates the root of each timestamp value using the specified index.Argument: arg (Decimal data type) – The index of the root. For example, the following returns the square root of each timestamp: "transforms": [ { "name": "root", "arg": "2" }, ]

params.name: stddev
params.text: Creates a series that contains the standard deviation of values for each timestamp across a set of series.

params.name: sub
params.text: Subtracts the specified number from the value in each timestamp.Argument: arg (Number) – The number to subtract from the value in each timestamp.

params.name: sum
params.text: Aggregates the selected metric series into one series that contains the sum of all values for each timestamp, excluding any NaNs. If all numbers in the series are NaN, the output is NaN.

params.name: timeshift
params.text: Shifts the time range by adding the specified offset to a value’s timestamp without modifying the value. Use this transform to shift timestamps to another timezone.Argument: arg (Duration data type) – The amount of time to shift by.

params.name: top
params.text: Returns the specified number of series that have the highest values.Argument: arg (Integer) – The number of series to return. For example, the following returns the two time series that contain the highest sets of values.

params.name: Aggregator
params.text: Available aggregators to use within the transform.- AVG: Calculates the arithmetic mean of all currently selected series. - CHISQUARE: Shows how well a statistical model fits the metric dataset. - LAST: Returns the last defined value in the period window.

params.name: DateTime
params.text: Absolute date/time values are specified by the ISO 8601 date and time format: YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss. For example: 2020-02-28T13:10:42.Where: - [YYYY]: Four-digit year. - [MM]: Zero-padded month between 01 and 12. - [DD]: Zero-padded day between 01 and 31.

params.name: Decimal
params.text: Decimal value that can either be: - A signed decimal number of arbitrary precision that can use exponential notation.

params.name: Duration
params.text: Amount of time in a time interval. Duration values are specified by the ISO 8601 duration format: P[n]Y[n]M[n]DT[n]H[n]M[n]S Where: - P: Duration designator, referred to as "period", and is always placed at the beginning of the duration.

params.text: Sys_id of a policy check sandbox copy in the Check Instances [sn_agent_check] table.

params.name: active
params.text: Flag that indicates whether the policy check is active.Valid values: - true: Policy check is active. - false: Policy check is inactive.

params.name: auto_generate
params.text: Flag that indicates whether to automatically generate the command with the command_prefix value.Valid values: - true: Automatically populate the command property with active parameter values. - false: Command isn't automatically generated.

params.name: check_type
params.text: Check type specifying the monitoring option.Possible values: - Discovery: Check that locates CIs related to the agent. - Events: The check's result is transformed into an Event Management event.

params.name: command
params.text: Command that the Agent Client Collector executes. Parameter taken from a template or monitored CI.Note: If auto_generate is true, this property is automatically populated with the prefix and flags of the active parameters listed in the parameters object.

params.name: command_prefix
params.text: If the auto_generate property is true, this command is used for automatic generation. The prefix consists of any portion of the command which is static (does not change), such as the script name.

params.name: event_status_change_threshold
params.text: Number of consecutive times that a check's response status must happen before a new event is sent.

params.name: event_status_repair_threshold
params.text: Number of consecutive times that a check's response status must improve to close the previous event. Returns null if not set.

params.name: interval
params.text: Amount of time in seconds to wait between check executions. For example, a value of 60 means that the check runs every 60 seconds.

params.name: timeout
params.text: Amount of time, in seconds, after which the check execution stops when no output is returned. For example, a value of 60 means that when the check execution doesn't return a value for 60 seconds, the execution stops.

params.text: Description

operations.summary: Submits a request to upload the passed-in configuration data for a specific component, within the system components folder, for the specified application.

params.name: appName
params.text: Name of the application to associate with the configuration data. This application must be in the active state.

params.name: autoCommit
params.text: Flag that indicates whether the changeset identified in the changesetNumber parameter is committed to the data model after upload.Valid values: - true: Changeset is committed after upload. - false: Changeset isn't committed after upload.

params.name: autoDelete
params.text: Flag that indicates whether the existing nodes, that aren’t part of the upload content, are deleted after the processing is complete.Valid values: - true: Automatically delete existing nodes. - false: Don't automatically delete existing nodes.

params.name: autoValidate
params.text: Flag that indicates whether the snapshots created when committed are validated.Valid values: - true: Validate the snapshots. - false: Don't validate the snapshots. Note: This option is only available if the autoCommit parameter is true.

params.name: changesetNumber
params.text: String that uniquely identifies the changeset associated with the application, such as Chset-102. This changeset must be in the "Open" state.Data type: String Default: Creates a changeset to use.

params.name: dataFormat
params.text: Format of the configuration data.Valid values: - csv - ini - json - properties - raw - xml - yaml

params.name: dataFormatAttributes
params.text: Only supported when the dataFormat parameter is set to csv. Attributes that define the CSV data format.

params.name: dataFormatAttributes.containsHeaders
params.text: Flag that indicates whether the data contains a header row.Valid values: - true: Data contains a header row. The first row in the data is considered the header row.

params.name: dataFormatAttributes.delimeter
params.text: Character to use to delineate fields within the data.

params.name: dataFormatAttributes.headers
params.text: Required if dataFormatAttributes.containsHeaders parameter is false. Fields in the data that comprise the header. These headers are converted to the key names of the CDIs in the JSON format. The number of headers must match the number of record fields.

params.name: dataFormatAttributes.securedHeaders
params.text: Fields in the data that are secure fields and must be encrypted in the data uploaded to CDM. The name of the secured headers must match the name of the headers in the headers attribute or data file.

params.name: deleteRedundantOverrides
params.text: Flag that indicates whether to create an override where redundant values are present.Valid values: - true: If redundant values are present, an override isn’t created. - false: If redundant values are present, proceeds with an override. Default: true

params.name: fileName
params.text: Name of the file to upload. This name can differ from than the actual file name and contain the file extension. For example, .txt/.scv/.jar. The fileName value is applied when downloading the file.

params.name: fileNodeName
params.text: Name of the file node. This file name is used in the configuration data when exporting it. This name doesn’t require a file extension nor does it affect the download.

params.name: identifierKeys
params.text: List of names that indicate which key in an array child to use to identify the same node.For example, if you’re uploading: [ {"name" : "Allan, "city" : "Paris"}, {"name" : "Karen, "city" : "Sydney"} ] in the following existing model: [ {"name" : "Karen,…

params.name: ignoreAttributes
params.text: Flag that indicates whether the given data format supports attributes (currently only XML).Valid values: - true: If the given data format supports attributes, any attributes in the input data are skipped during the upload.

params.name: namePath
params.text: Path of the targeted node under which the configuration data should be uploaded. This path is relative to the components, collection, or deployable folder (depending on the endpoint being called).You can pass the name path in any of the following formats.

params.name: sharedLibraryName
params.text: Name of the shared library where the component to delete is located.

name: virtual-agent-bot
title: Virtual Agent Bot Integration API
text: The Virtual Agent Bot Integration API provides endpoints that allow users to integrate any chat interface or a bot ecosystem with the ServiceNow Virtual Agent and/or Live Agent.Sends a specified…

operations.summary: Sends a specified message, attachment, or URL to a specified secondary ServiceNow Virtual Agent (VA) bot.

params.name: action
params.text: Action that the VA should take.Valid values: - AGENT: Switches the conversation from VA to Live Agent. - CREATE_CONVERSATION: Creates a chat interaction. Set syncResponse to true to process the request synchronously and eliminate timing issues.

params.name: botToBot
params.text: Flag that indicates whether the conversation is between bots, such as between a primary bot and secondary bot.Possible values: - true: Bot-to-bot conversation. - false: Standalone ServiceNow bot conversation.

params.name: cause
params.text: Cause of a chat conversation fault, for example, EXTERNAL_FAILURE. This property is only used when the action property is set to FAULT_CONVERSATION.

params.name: clientSessionId
params.text: Unique client session identifier of the application/service that the end user is using to communicate with the ServiceNow botor the supported third-party chat applications.- This ID helps identify the set of request/responses for a specific user conversation.

params.name: clientVariables
params.text: Pass-through JSON-formatted name-value pairs that are sent back in the response. These values aren't processed by the endpoint, but can be used to keep specific customer information attached to the conversation.

params.name: contextVariables
params.text: JSON-formatted name-value pairs that provide addition information about the user. Provide this information to customize the conversation experience.

params.name: emailId
params.text: Required when enabling account linking, otherwise all users are considered guest users. Email address of the chat client end user, the person the bot is interacting with.

params.name: history
params.text: History of the primary bot’s conversation with the user, starting with the initial request by the user.Data type: Object "history": { "attachment": {Object}, "displayName": "String", "isBotMessage": Boolean, "timestamp": "String", "type": "String", "value":…

fields.name: attachment
fields.text: Required when history.type is attachment (ignored if history.type is text). Details of each attachment sent in the historical message.Only a single attachment is allowed per attachment object.

fields.name: clientAttachmentId
fields.text: Unique identifier of the attachment. The format of this identifier is determined by the implementer.

fields.name: contentType
fields.text: Required if history.attachment is specified. Standard mime type of the attachment. Valid values (not case-sensitive): - application/pdf - application/msword - image/png - image/jpeg - text/plain - video/mpeg

fields.name: fileName
fields.text: Required if history.attachment is specified. File name of the attachment.

fields.name: headers
fields.text: Additional information needed if the attachment file is private and protected.

fields.name: Authorization
fields.text: Information needed to obtain authorization to access the attachment if it is private and protected, such as a user name and password.

fields.name: url
fields.text: Required if history.attachment is specified. URL where the attachment is located.If the attachment isn't a public file, you must pass a history.attachment.headers object that contains the authorization information so that the attachment can be accessed.

fields.name: displayName
fields.text: Name of the user to whom the message was sent. If the primary bot, pass Bot.

fields.name: isBotMessage
fields.text: Flag that indicates whether the message was sent by the primary bot.Valid values: - true: Message was sent by the primary bot. - false: Message was sent by the user.

fields.name: timestamp
fields.text: Timestamp indicating the time at which the message was sent in milliseconds.Valid values: 13-digit Unix timestamp

fields.name: type
fields.text: Type of message sent.Valid values: - text - attachment

fields.name: value
fields.text: Content of the information. For example, the message text. Ignored when history.type is attachment.

params.name: intent
params.text: Describes the intent of the conversation. Provide this information when the action parameter is set to SWITCH.

fields.name: id
fields.text: NLU Intent ID of the system topic to switch the conversation to. The intent.id is resolved based on the language passed in the chat session. If no language is passed when starting a conversation, it obtains the language from the user's session/profile.

params.name: message
params.text: Details of the message to send to the ServiceNow bot.Data type: Object "message": { "attachment": [Array of Objects], "clientMessageId": "String", "status": "String", "text": "String", "typed": Boolean }

fields.name: attachment
fields.text: Required if sending attachments. Details of each attachment to send.You can only pass attachments as a URL. A virus scan is triggered on all attachments.

fields.name: clientAttachmentId
fields.text: Unique identifier of the attachment to send to the ServiceNow bot. The format of this identifier is determined by the implementer.

fields.name: contentType
fields.text: Required if attachment specified. Standard mime type of the attachment.Valid values (not case-sensitive): - application/pdf - application/msword - image/png - image/jpeg - text/plain - video/mpeg

fields.name: fileName
fields.text: Required if attachment specified. File name of the attachment.

fields.name: headers
fields.text: Additional information needed if the attachment file is private and protected.

fields.name: Authorization
fields.text: Information needed to obtain authorization to access the attachment, such as a user name and password.

fields.name: url
fields.text: Required if attachment specified. URL where the attachment is located. The VA obtains the attachment from this URL, runs a virus scan, and then processes the file.

fields.name: clientMessageId
fields.text: Unique alphanumeric identifier for the message. The format of this identifier is determined by the implementer.

fields.name: id
fields.text: Only used with the UPDATE_MESSAGES action. Unique ID of the chat message to be updated.

fields.name: status
fields.text: Message status.Valid values (not case-sensitive): - external_error - Used when message delivery is failed from third-party chat integration to end user. The agent chat panel will be reflected as a "Failed" tag.

fields.name: text
fields.text: Required if attachment parameter isn't specified. Message text. - The language of the message should be passed in the contextVariables parameter. - Must be empty if the value of the action property is END_CONVERSATION.

fields.name: typed
fields.text: Flag that indicates whether the message was typed in or was an option selection (selected).Valid values: - true: Message was typed in by the user. - false: Message was an option selection.

params.name: requestId
params.text: Unique alphanumeric identifier for this request. The format of this identifier is determined by the implementer.

params.name: silentMessage
params.text: Flag that indicates whether this is a silent message. A silent message is a message that doesn’t require a response.Valid values: - true: Silent message, no response message expected. - false: Regular message, response message expected.

params.name: syncResponse
params.text: Applicable for CREATE_CONVERSATION and START_CREATED_CONVERSATION actions. Flag that indicates whether to wait before returning a synchronous response from the API.

params.name: timestamp
params.text: Unix epoch time when the message was sent from the end user of the chat client.

params.name: timezone

name: scorecards
title: Scorecards API
text: The Scorecards API provides endpoints that enable you to query data about Performance Analytics indicators.

operations.summary: Retrieves details about indicators from the Analytics Hub.

params.name: sysparm_breakdown
params.text: Sys_id of a breakdown to return chart information organized as defined by the breakdown.

params.name: sysparm_breakdown_relation
params.text: Sys_id of a breakdown relation to break down the returned data using that relation.

params.name: sysparm_contains
params.text: Comma-separated list of names or descriptions to return results only from indicators with a matching value. All the comma-separated list items must match, or no results are returned: The list follows AND logic, not OR logic.

params.name: sysparm_display
params.text: Flag that indicates the type of indicators to return.Valid values: - true: Return only indicators that display on the Analytics Hub. - all: Return all indicators.

params.name: sysparm_display_value
params.text: Determines the type of data returned, either the actual values from the database or the display values of the fields.

params.name: sysparm_elements_filter
params.text: Sys_id of an elements filter to apply to the returned data.

params.name: sysparm_exclude_reference_link
params.text: Flag that indicates whether to hide additional information provided for reference fields, such as the URI to the reference resource.Valid values: - true: Hide additional information provided for reference fields.

params.name: sysparm_favorites
params.text: Flag that indicates whether to return only indicators that are favorites of the querying user.Valid values: - true: Return only indicators that are favorites of the querying user. - false: Return all indicators.

params.name: sysparm_from
params.text: Earliest date to return scores from. Only scores from this date or later are returned. This parameter requires that include_scores is set to true. Format: ISO-8601 standard Date type: String

params.name: sysparm_include_aggregates
params.text: Flag that indicates whether to return all possible aggregates for an indicator, including aggregates that have already been applied.Valid values: - true: Return all possible aggregates for an indicator, including aggregates that have already been applied.

params.name: sysparm_include_available_aggregates
params.text: Flag that indicates whether to return all available aggregates for an indicator when no aggregate has been applied.Valid values: - true: Return all available aggregates for an indicator when no aggregate has been applied. - false: Return no aggregates.

params.name: sysparm_include_available_breakdowns
params.text: Flag that indicates whether to return all available breakdowns for an indicator.Valid values: - true: Return all available breakdowns for an indicator. - false: Return no breakdowns.

params.name: sysparm_include_forecast_scores
params.text: Flag that indicates whether to return the forecast_scores element that contains an array of date-value pairs that define the forecast data for the Analytics Hub. This parameter requires that the include_scores parameter is also set to true.

params.name: sysparm_include_realtime
params.text: Flag that indicates whether to return the realtime_enabled element which indicates if real-time scores are enabled for the indicator, and the realtime_value element which contains the real-time score value.

params.name: sysparm_include_score_notes
params.text: Flag that indicates whether to return all notes associated with the score. The note element contains the note text as well as the author and timestamp when the note was added.Valid values: - true: Return all notes associated with the score.

params.name: sysparm_include_scores
params.text: Flag that indicates whether to return indicator scores for the entire time range selected on the Analytics Hub. If a value is not specified, this parameter defaults to false and returns only the most recent score value.

params.name: sysparm_include_target_color_scheme
params.text: Flag that indicates whether to return the target_color_scheme element that contains the minimum and maximum values, and the color of each section of the target color scheme for the Analytics Hub.Valid values: - true: Return the target_color_scheme element.

params.name: sysparm_include_trendline_scores
params.text: Flag that indicates whether to return the trendline_scores element that contains an array of date-value pairs that define the Analytics Hub trendline. This parameter requires that the include_scores parameter is also set to true.

params.name: sysparm_key
params.text: Flag that indicates whether to return results only for key indicators.Valid values: - true: Return the trendline_scores element. - false: Do not return the trendline_scores element .

params.name: sysparm_limit
params.text: Maximum number of scores to return.

params.name: sysparm_page
params.text: Page number. For example, when querying 20 indicators with the default sysparm_per_page value (10), specify a sysparm_page value of 2 to retrieve indicators 11-20.

params.name: sysparm_per_page
params.text: Maximum number of indicators each query can return on a page.Default: 10 Maximum: 100

params.name: sysparm_sortby
params.text: Value to use when sorting results.Valid values: - bullet - change - changeperc - date - default - direction - duedate - frequency - gap - gapperc - group - indicator_group - name - order - target - trend - value

params.name: sysparm_sortdir
params.text: Sort direction.Valid values: - asc: Denotes ascending - des: Denotes descending

params.name: sysparm_step
params.text: Numeric value to skip scores, based on the indicator frequency. For example, specify a value of 3 to return only scores from every third day for a daily indicator, or from every third week for a weekly indicator.

params.name: sysparm_tags
params.text: Indicator group sys_id in which to return the indicators of that group. Do not use sysparm_uuid with this parameter.You cannot obtain the sys_id of an indicator group through this API. Instead, get the sys_id from the indicator group record.

params.name: sysparm_target
params.text: Flag that indicates whether to return results only for indicators that have a target set on the Analytics Hub.Valid values: - true: Only return results for indicators that have a target set. - false: Return results for all applicable indicators.

params.name: sysparm_to
params.text: Latest date from which to return scores. Only scores from this date or earlier are returned. This parameter requires that include_scores is set to true.

params.name: sysparm_uuid
params.text: Colon-separated list of sys_id values to specify which indicators, breakdowns, aggregates, and domains to query.

params.text: Message Control ID. Echoed back in the MSA.2 field of the ACK response.

operations.summary: Provides actions for integrating third-party Contact Center as a Service (CCaaS) platforms with ServiceNow®'s Omnichannel Callback system.

params.name: Object
params.text: Object containing the operation and details.

params.name: action
params.text: Defines the action to perform on the callback.Accepted values: - create: Creates a new callback record. - update: Updates an existing callback record based on the callback number.

params.name: payload
params.text: Object containing specific data required for the given action when routingContext object is passed.

fields.name: callbackContext
fields.text: Object containing the context details about the callback request.Table: Callback Context [sys_cs_callback_context]

fields.name: customer_timezone
fields.text: Time zone of customer who requested the callback. Time zones can be provided in the following formats. - Country/City. For example, America/Los_Angeles. - Country/Time zone. For example, US/Pacific. - Time zone abbreviation. For example, PST.

fields.name: ivr_path
fields.text: The IVR (Interactive Voice Response) path that a customer follows before being transferred to a human agent.Typically contains a list of queues or menu options the customer navigated through in the IVR system.

fields.name: queue
fields.text: Number assignments in the queue.

fields.name: callbackDetails
fields.text: Object containing the details about the callback request.Table: Callback [sys_cs_callback] Data type: Object "callbackDetails": { "description": "String", "end_time": "String", "expire_time": "String", "first_name": "String", "last_name": "String",…

fields.name: description
fields.text: Detailed explanation of the callback request. Can include specific customer concerns, context, or notes from the agent.

fields.name: end_time
fields.text: The time window when the callback request is expected to be completed. After this timestamp, the callback is considered overdue or expired unless rescheduled.

fields.name: expire_time
fields.text: The final cutoff time after which the callback request should no longer be attempted. This is often used to automatically close or cancel stale requests.Format: glide_date_time value, such as yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss

fields.name: first_name
fields.text: First name of the customer requesting the callback.

fields.name: last_name
fields.text: Last name of the customer requesting the callback.

fields.name: opened_by
fields.text: Sys_id of the user or agent who created or initiated the callback request.

fields.name: phone_number
fields.text: Phone number of the customer to call back.

fields.name: next_retry
fields.text: The next scheduled attempt time if previous callback attempts were unsuccessful. Useful for automated or manual retry logic.Format: glide_date_time value, such as yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss

fields.name: reason
fields.text: Reason for the callback request. Helps with routing, analytics, and reporting by tagging the callback with a standardized reason.Valid values: - Other issue - Custom values defined by your implementation. For example, “Billing Inquiry”, “Technical Support”

fields.name: scheduled_start_time
fields.text: Date and time value to when the callback window begins. Only applicable to a Scheduled callback type.Format: glide_date_time value, such as yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss

fields.name: short_description
fields.text: A brief summary of the callback request, usually used in lists or dashboards.

fields.name: state
fields.text: The current workflow status of the callback request. Valid values: - pending approval - in progress - completed - canceled

fields.name: type
fields.text: The category of the request. Value is always callback.

fields.name: callbackId
fields.text: Sys_id or external_id of the callback.

fields.name: phoneNumber
fields.text: Phone number of the user requesting the callback.

fields.name: type

name: product-offering-qualification
title: Product Offering Qualification API
text: The Product Offering Qualification API determines eligibility for product offerings in the ServiceNow product catalog, scoped to a customer account, sales channel, and geographic location.

operations.summary: Synchronously evaluates one or more product offerings for eligibility. Returns green (eligible) or red (ineligible) per item, with structured reasons for ineligible items.

params.name: channel
params.text: Sales channel through which the customer is interacting (for example, "web"). When provided, the eligibility engine applies any channel-specific eligibility rules.

fields.name: id
fields.text: Choice value identifying the channel. Mandatory when channel is present. This is the value field from the sys_choice table for the channel field, not a sys_id. An empty string is rejected with a 400 validation error. Example: "web"

fields.name: type
fields.text: Discriminator for the channel object. Mandatory when channel is present. Set to "ChannelRef".

params.name: checkProductOfferingQualificationItem
params.text: List of product offerings to evaluate for eligibility. Must contain at least one entry.Each element is a CheckProductOfferingQualificationItem object that identifies a specific product offering and optionally provides location context.

fields.name: @type
fields.text: Discriminator for the item object. Set to "CheckProductOfferingQualificationItem". Informational; the API does not enforce this value but it's recommended for TMF compliance.

fields.name: place
fields.text: Geographic location context scoped to this individual item. Use this to supply the service or billing address for location-based eligibility rules. Each entry in the array represents one location with a role (e.g.

fields.name: @type
fields.text: Mandatory when a place entry is present. Discriminator for the place wrapper. Set to "Place".

fields.name: role
fields.text: Conditional. Mandatory when a place entry is present. Valid values: serviceLocation, billingLocation.

fields.name: productOffering
fields.text: Reference to the product offering to evaluate. The eligibility engine looks up this offering in the Product Catalog by its id.

fields.name: @type
fields.text: Discriminator for the product offering reference. Set to "ProductOfferingRef". Informational; recommended for TMF compliance.

fields.name: id
fields.text: Sys_id or external ID of the offering. When an external ID maps to multiple versions, the latest version is used for evaluation. If the ID does not resolve to a known offering, the item is returned as ineligible ("red") with an eligibility reason.

params.name: checkProductOfferingQualificationItem.place.place.@type
params.text: Determines how the location is identified. Mandatory when a place entry is present. Two values are supported:- "PlaceRef": Reference to an existing Location record in the instance. Provide only the id field; no other address fields are permitted.

params.name: checkProductOfferingQualificationItem.place.place.city
params.text: City name for the inline geographic address. Only applicable when @type is "GeographicAddress". Used by location-based eligibility rules to match service territories.Example: "San Diego"

params.name: checkProductOfferingQualificationItem.place.place.country
params.text: Country name or ISO country code. Only applicable when @type is "GeographicAddress".Example: "US", "France"

params.name: checkProductOfferingQualificationItem.place.place.id
params.text: Sys_id of the Location record in the instance. Required when @type is "PlaceRef". Must refer to an existing Location record; an unresolved ID causes the item to be returned as ineligible ("red"). Must not be provided when @type is "GeographicAddress".

params.name: checkProductOfferingQualificationItem.place.place.postcode
params.text: Postal or ZIP code. Only applicable when @type is "GeographicAddress". Eligibility rules can use this for postcode-based service territory matching.Example: "92101", "75001"

params.name: checkProductOfferingQualificationItem.place.place.stateOrProvince
params.text: State or province name. Only applicable when @type is "GeographicAddress".Example: "CA", "California"

params.name: checkProductOfferingQualificationItem.place.place.streetName
params.text: Street name without the number. Only applicable when @type is "GeographicAddress". When streetNumber is also provided, the API combines them as "{streetNumber} {streetName}" for eligibility rule matching.Example: "Main St"

params.name: checkProductOfferingQualificationItem.place.place.streetNumber
params.text: Street number. Prepended to streetName when present.Example: "123"

params.name: relatedParty
params.text: Identifies the customer account for which qualification is being checked. Must contain at least one entry. The eligibility engine uses the referenced account to apply customer-specific eligibility rules (for example, existing subscriptions, customer segment).

fields.name: @type
fields.text: Discriminator for this related party entry. Set to "RelatedParty".

fields.name: partyOrPartyRole
fields.text: The account reference nested inside the related party. Contains the @type discriminator and the id that identifies the customer account.

fields.name: @type
fields.text: Discriminator for the account reference. Mandatory when partyOrPartyRole is present. Must be exactly "AccountRef". Any other value (for example, "IndividualRef") causes the API to return a 400 error because only account-based eligibility is supported.

fields.name: id
fields.text: Sys_id of the customer account record. Mandatory when partyOrPartyRole is present. The eligibility engine loads this account to apply account-level eligibility rules. The request is rejected with a 400 if the account does not exist.

params.text: Description

params.name: Content-Type
params.text: application/json

operations.summary: Discovers eligible product offerings for a given customer, channel, and location context. Supports category filtering and pagination via limit and offset query parameters.

params.name: limit
params.text: Max number of items to return. Non-numeric value or value exceeding MAX_LIMIT returns a 404 error.Data type: String Default: 20 (configurable via the sn_tmf_api.pagination.set_limit system parameter.) Maximum: 100 (configurable via the…

params.name: offset
params.text: Zero-based index of the first result. Non-numeric value or value ≥ totalCount (when totalCount > 0) returns a 404 error.

params.name: @type
params.text: TMF discriminator for the request body. Set to "QueryProductOfferingQualification". Informational; recommended for TMF conformance.

params.name: category
params.text: Filters the catalog query to a specific product category. When provided, only offerings that belong to the referenced category are evaluated and returned. This is useful for building category-specific storefronts or ServiceNow CPQ catalog panels.

fields.name: @type
fields.text: Conditional. Discriminator for the category reference. Mandatory when category is present. Set to "CategoryRef".

fields.name: id
fields.text: Conditional. Sys_id of the Product Category record. Mandatory when category is provided. The API filters the catalog to offerings linked to this category. A non-existent ID returns a 400 validation error.

params.name: channel
params.text: Identifies the sales channel for this query. When provided, the eligibility engine applies channel-specific rules and may restrict results to offerings available through this channel. The channel is also echoed back in the response.

fields.name: @type
fields.text: Conditional. Discriminator for the channel object. Mandatory when channel is present. Set to "ChannelRef".

fields.name: id
fields.text: Conditional. The choice value identifying the channel. Mandatory when channel is present. This is the value field from the sys_choice table for the channel field (for example, "web"), not a sys_id. An empty string is rejected with a 400 validation error.

fields.name: name
fields.text: Display name of the channel. Informational; echoed back in the response.Example: "Web", "Retail"

params.name: relatedParty
params.text: Identifies the customer account for which the catalog query is run. The eligibility engine uses this account to apply customer-segment and account-level eligibility rules; results are personalized to this customer. Must contain at least one entry.

fields.name: @type
fields.text: Discriminator for this related party entry. Set to "RelatedPartyOrPartyRole". Used to validate the entry structure.

fields.name: partyOrPartyRole
fields.text: The account reference nested inside the related party. Contains the discriminator and the sys_id of the customer account to qualify against.

fields.name: @type
fields.text: Conditional. Discriminator for the account reference. Mandatory when partyOrPartyRole is present. Must be exactly "AccountRef".Only account-based eligibility is supported. Any other value returns a 400 error.

fields.name: id
fields.text: Conditional. Sys_id of the customer account record. Mandatory when partyOrPartyRole is present. The eligibility engine loads this account to evaluate account-level eligibility rules. A non-existent account ID returns a 400 error.

fields.name: role
fields.text: Describes the role of the related party in this query. Must not be empty.Used by the eligibility engine to interpret the party's relationship to the qualification request. A missing or empty value returns a 400 validation error. Example: "requester""customer"

params.name: searchCriteria
params.text: Container for location-based search filters. When provided, the eligibility engine uses the nested place array to restrict results to offerings available at the specified geographic location(s).The entire searchCriteria object is echoed back in the response.

fields.name: @type
fields.text: Discriminator for the searchCriteria object. Typically set to "QueryProductOfferingQualification". Informational; echoed in the response.

fields.name: place
fields.text: List of location constraints for the query. The eligibility engine filters the catalog to offerings that are available at all provided locations.At most one entry per role value — one serviceLocation and one billingLocation.

fields.name: @type
fields.text: Conditional. Mandatory when a place entry is present. Discriminator for the place wrapper object. Set to "Place".

fields.name: place
fields.text: The location reference, either a PlaceRef or GeographicAddress.Data type: Object "place": { "@type": "String", "streetName": "String", "streetNumber": "String", "city": "String", "postcode": "String", "country": "String" }

fields.name: @type
fields.text: Conditional. Determines how the location is identified. Mandatory when a place entry is present. Valid values: - PlaceRef: Reference to an existing Location record. Only id is permitted; no other address fields may be present.

fields.name: city
fields.text: City name. Only applicable when @type is "GeographicAddress". Used by location-based eligibility rules to match service territories.Example: "Paris", "San Diego"

fields.name: country
fields.text: Country name or ISO code. Only applicable when @type is "GeographicAddress".Example: "France", "US"

fields.name: id

fields.name: alert_severity
fields.text: Severity level of alerts created for failed monitor tests. Only use this parameter if checks.should_create_alert is set to true.Valid values: - 1: Critical - 2: Major - 3: Minor - 4: Warning - 5: OK Default: 1

fields.name: alert_tags
fields.text: Custom tags to use for alerts created for failed monitor tests. Only use this parameter if checks.should_create_alert is set to true.The elements contained in this object vary based on the tags used.

fields.name: body
fields.text: Request body for POST, PUT, or PATCH endpoints. Must be a valid JSON or XML string depending on the Content-Type header. Maximum size is 10KB.Default: Null

fields.name: body_condition
fields.text: Response body validation.

fields.name: expression
fields.text: Expression to check the response body against. The expression can be any string value, including support for regex, JSONPath, and XPath.Default: Null

fields.name: type
fields.text: Type of validation used to evaluate the response body against checks.body_condition.expression.Valid values (case-sensitive): - equals: Exact match. - not_equals: Not equal to. - contains: Contains substring. - not_contains: Does not contain substring.

fields.name: cmdb_ci
fields.text: Sys_id of the CMDB endpoint configuration item (CI) or endpoint URL.If a URL is provided that matches an existing endpoint CI, that CI is used for the monitor.

fields.name: credential
fields.text: Sys_id of the credential for the monitor to include in the endpoint request.

fields.name: description
fields.text: Description of the monitor.

fields.name: enabled
fields.text: Flag that indicates whether the monitor will start executing immediately after creation.Valid values: - true: The monitor starts executing immediately after creation. - false: The monitor won't start executing until it is enabled. Default: true

fields.name: headers
fields.text: Array of HTTP headers for the monitor to include in the endpoint request.

fields.name: name
fields.text: Name of the HTTP header, such as Authorization or Content-Type.

fields.name: value
fields.text: Value of the HTTP header, such as Bearer token or application/json.

fields.name: interval
fields.text: Frequency of monitor execution in minutes.ServiceNow hosted locations are limited to 6 tests per minute per monitor. Valid values: 1-60 For example, a value of 5 sets the monitor to execute once every five minutes.

fields.name: locations
fields.text: List of sys_ids of MID Server locations to use for the monitor.

fields.name: max_latency_ms
fields.text: Maximum acceptable response time in milliseconds. The general guideline is 500-5000ms depending on the endpoint type. The monitor checks against this value when testing, and the test fails if the response time exceeds this value.

fields.name: method
fields.text: HTTP method to use. Valid values (case-insensitive): - DELETE - GET - HEAD - PATCH - POST - PUT

fields.name: name
fields.text: Display name for the monitor.Maximum length: 100 characters

fields.name: parent_service_sys_id
fields.text: Required unless the endpoint has a parent service relationship in the CI Relationship [cmdb_rel_ci] table. Sys_id of the business service this endpoint supports. Used for service-level reporting and impact analysis.

fields.name: query_string
fields.text: Query parameters for the monitor to include in the endpoint request.Default: Null

fields.name: should_create_alert
fields.text: Flag that indicates whether the monitor will create an alert if a test fails.Valid values: - true: Alerts are created if monitor tests fail. - false: Alerts aren't created if monitor tests fail. Default: false

fields.name: single_api_check_sys_id
fields.text: Sys_id of the monitor for the endpoint. Use this parameter to update an existing monitor.

fields.name: support_group_sys_id
fields.text: Required unless the endpoint has a parent service relationship in the CI Relationship [cmdb_rel_ci] table. Sys_id of the support group responsible for this endpoint. Used for alert routing and assignment.

fields.name: valid_http_code
fields.text: Expected HTTP status codes for a successful response. Valid formats: - Single value, such as 200. - Range of values, such as 200-202. - Comma-separated list of values, such as '200,201,204'. - Regular expression, such as 2[0-9]{2} (matches codes 200-299).

fields.name: valid_http_code_type
fields.text: Type of validation used to check the HTTP status code from a response.Valid values (case-sensitive): - equals: Checks for an exact match with checks.valid_http_code.

params.name: recurringPattern
params.text: Details about the recurring pattern for the reservation.Data type: Object "recurringPattern": { "freq": "String", "interval": Number, "dtstart": "String", "until": "String", "byweekday": [Array], "duration": Number, "tzid": "String" }

fields.name: bymonthday
fields.text: Conditional. Required if freq is MONTHLY, unless using bysetpos + byweekday. Day of the month for the occurrence. Valid values: - 1–31 - or -1 for last day of month. Mutually exclusive with bysetpos.

fields.name: bysetpos
fields.text: Conditional Used together with byweekday for "nth weekday of month" patterns (for example, 2nd Monday). Valid values: - 1 - 2 - 3 - 4 - -1 ( = last). Mutually exclusive with bymonthday.

fields.name: byweekday
fields.text: Conditional. Required if freq is WEEKLY. Days of the week that the reservable is needed. Also used with bysetpos for monthly "nth weekday" patterns.

fields.name: count
fields.text: Conditional. Number of occurrences to generate. Mutually exclusive with until — exactly one of until or count is required.

fields.name: dtstart
fields.text: Start date and time for the recurring pattern, expressed as local wall-clock time in the timezone specified by freq. Do not include a Z suffix — the value represents the local time at the building.

fields.name: duration
fields.text: Required (except shift-based reservations). Length of time to reserve the reservable, in milliseconds. For example, 3600000 = 1 hour.

fields.name: freq
fields.text: Repeating frequency for the reservation. Valid values (case-sensitive): - DAILY - WEEKLY - MONTHLY - YEARLY

fields.name: interval
fields.text: Pattern repeat interval. For example, the value 2 indicates that the pattern repeats every 2 days or 2 months depending on the value of freq.

fields.name: tzid
fields.text: IANA timezone name for the building where the reservation is located. All date and time values in the pattern (dtstart, until) must be expressed as local wall-clock time in this timezone.The system uses this timezone to generate occurrences with correct…

fields.name: until
fields.text: Conditional. End date boundary for the recurrence, expressed as local wall-clock time in the timezone specified by tzid. Mutually exclusive with count — exactly one of until or count is required.

text: The Workplace Service Delivery (WSD) Search API provides endpoints to search for available locations and workplace items such as reservables, reservable modules, and available shifts.Checks whether…

operations.summary: Checks whether the specified reservables are available for the specified times.

params.name: end
params.text: End time to use to search for available reservable modules. This value must be later than the value specified in the start parameter.

params.name: include_reservations_within_days
params.text: Flag that indicates whether to return all free slots of available times in the response for each reservable for the whole day.Valid values: - true: Return all free slots. - false: Don't return all free slots.

params.name: reservable_ids
params.text: Comma-separated list of reservable sys_ids to evaluate for availability.

params.name: reservation_ids
params.text: Comma-separated list of existing reservation sys_ids. Pass this parameter if you want to edit the associated reservations.The time blocked for these sys_ids for the corresponding reservables are treated as available.

params.name: reservable_module
params.text: Sys_id of the reservable module to include in the search. A reservable module groups similar types of workplace items.

params.name: schedule_view_obj
params.text: Details about the schedule view to return. Pass this object if you need 24-hour availability data for reservations that span more than one day.

params.name: schedule_view_obj.schedule_view_date
params.text: Date for which to start returning reservation availability. This date must be in the time zone specified in the schedule_view_obj.timezone parameter.

params.name: schedule_view_obj.timezone
params.text: Building time zone to use to determine the reservation availability data to return. For example: US/Pacific.

params.name: shift
params.text: Required if the specified reservable modules are based on a shift. Conditional. Sys_id of the shift to associate with the reservation. If this parameter is passed in, the end parameter isn't required.

params.name: start
params.text: Start time to use to search for available reservable modules. This value must be prior to the value specified in the end parameter.

params.name: best_match_count
params.text: Number of best matched reservables to return.

params.name: end

params.name: include_reservable_purposes

params.text: Flag that indicates whether to return all free slots of available times in the response for each reservable for the whole day.Valid values: - true: Return all free slots. - false: Don't return all free slots.

params.name: include_standard_​services

params.name: q

params.name: reservable_module
params.text: Sys_id of the reservable module to include in the search. A reservable module groups similar types of workplace items.

params.name: start

params.name: time_slot
params.text: Sys_id of a time slot record for which we are trying to look for the best matching reservable.

params.name: timezone
params.text: Preferred time zone, such as Europe/Amsterdam.

operations.summary: Determines whether an overlapping reservation exists based on the passed parameters.

params.name: end
params.text: End time to use to check for overlapping reservations.

params.name: recurring_pattern
params.text: Details about the recurring pattern for the reservation.

params.name: recurring_pattern.duration
params.text: Length of time to check.

params.name: recurring_pattern.options
params.text: Details about the options associated with the recurring reservation.

params.name: recurring_pattern.options.count
params.text: Number of times the pattern is repeated.

params.name: recurring_pattern.options.daysOfWeek
params.text: Days of the week to check for overlap.Valid values: - 1 = Monday - 2 = Tuesday - 3 = Wednesday - 4 = Thursday - 5 = Friday - 6 = Saturday - 7 = Sunday For example, to specify Tuesday, Thursday, and Friday, pass 245 (no delimiter).

params.name: recurring_pattern.options.every
params.text: Pattern repeat interval to check. For example, if this value is 2, it checks the repeat pattern based on the selection in the repeats parameter, such as every other day or every other week.

params.name: recurring_pattern.options.repeats
params.text: Repeating pattern for the reservation overlap check.Possible values: (case-sensitive) - daily - monthly - weekly - yearly

params.name: reservable_id
params.text: Sys_id of the reservable module to check for overlapping reservations.

params.name: reservation_id
params.text: Sys_id of the reservation to check for overlap. This value is needed in the edit flow of multi/group parents.

params.name: shift_info_object
params.text: Details of the shift to check for overlap. For additional information on shift-based reservations, see Enable shift-based reservation.

params.name: shift_info_object.applyToShift
params.text: Flag that indicates whether shift-based reservations are enabled for the reservable module. Valid values: - true: Allow shift-based reservations. - false: Don't allow shift-based reservations.

params.name: shift_info_object.shift
params.text: Sys_id of the shift to associate with the reservation. If this parameter is passed in, the end parameter isn't required.

params.name: shift_info_object.timezone
params.text: Time zone of the shift to check for overlap.

params.name: start
params.text: Start time to use to check for overlapping reservations.

params.name: user_id
params.text: Sys_id of the user to check for overlapping reservations.

operations.summary: Searches for available reservable items using a specified reservable model configuration.

params.name: end
params.text: End time to use to search for available reservable modules. This value must be later than the value specified in the start parameter.

params.name: exclude_reservables
params.text: List of one or more sys_ids of reservables to exclude from the search results.Data type: String or Array Table: The table in which these sys_ids are located is specified in the reservable_table field in the Reservable Module [sn_wsd_rsv_reservable_module]…

params.name: ignore_same_day_validation
params.text: Flag that indicates whether the reservation search ignores the change of the date validation between the start and end parameters.Valid values: - true: Ignore the change date validation. - false: Don't ignore the change date validation.

params.name: include_reservable_purposes
params.text: Flag that indicates whether to return the purpose of reserving the workplace location for each reservable in the return results.Valid values: - true: Return the reservable purposes. - false: Don't return the reservable purposes.

params.name: include_reservations_within_days
params.text: Flag that indicates whether to return all free slots of available times in the response for each reservable for the whole day.Valid values: - true: Return all free slots. - false: Don't return all free slots.

params.name: include_standard_​services
params.text: Flag that indicates whether to return the standard services information in the response.

params.name: near_by_location_id
params.text: Required if the rsv_path parameter is set to browse_near_a_person. Sys_id of the location to use in the encoded query.

params.name: neighborhood
params.text: Required if the rsv_path parameter is set to browse_by_neighborhood. Only available if the Space Management (sn_wsd_spc_mgmt_neighborhood) plugin is activated. Sys_id of the neighborhood record to use in the encoded query.

params.name: next_item_index
params.text: Index of next item to retrieve. Pass this parameter when paginating the return results.

params.name: page_size
params.text: Maximum number of records to return in the return results.

params.name: q
params.text: Encoded query to use to filter the search return results. Within this query you must specify the building sys_id and you can specify parameters such as floor, area, capacity, standard services, and reservable_purposes.All passed parameters must be sys_ids,…

params.name: reservable_module
params.text: Sys_id of the reservable module to include in the search. A reservable module groups similar types of workplace items.

params.name: reservation_ids
params.text: Comma-separated list of existing reservation sys_ids. Pass this parameter if you want to edit the associated reservations.The time blocked for these sys_ids for the corresponding reservables are treated as available.

params.name: rsv_path
params.text: Reservation path to apply to the search.Valid values: - browse_all: Search all reservables. - browse_by_area: Search the reservables near a specific location. An area identifier must be passed in the encoded query (q parameter).

params.name: schedule_view_obj
params.text: Details about the schedule view to return. Pass this object if you need 24-hour availability data for reservations that span more than one day.

params.name: schedule_view_obj.schedule_view_date
params.text: Date for which to start returning reservation availability. This date must be in the time zone specified in the schedule_view_obj.timezone parameter.

params.name: schedule_view_obj.timezone
params.text: Building time zone to use to determine the reservation availability data to return. For example: US/Pacific.

params.name: start
params.text: Start time to use to search for available reservable modules. This value must be prior to the value specified in the end parameter.

params.name: shift
params.text: Conditional. Sys_id of the shift to associate with the reservation. If this parameter is passed in, the end parameter isn't required. For additional information on shift-based reservations, see Enable shift-based reservation.

params.name: sort_by
params.text: Desired sort order of the returned reservable items. Valid values: - a_z: Ascending sort order. - favorites_first: Sorted by the user's favorite workplace reservables first, ascending for the rest. - z_a: Descending sort order.

params.name: timezone
params.text: Preferred time zone, such as Europe/Amsterdam.

operations.summary: Returns an availability score for reservable items for specified timeslots.

params.name: recurringPattern
params.text: Required if startEndDateTimes parameter is not specified. Recurring pattern to use to search for reservables that are available for the specified recurring events.Data type: Object "recurringPattern": { "duration": Number, "label": "String", "options":…

fields.name: duration
fields.text: Length of time for which the reservable must be available.

fields.name: label
fields.text: Description of the recurring pattern, such as Repeats daily, 5 times.

fields.name: options
fields.text: Availability options for the recurring reservation to search for.

fields.name: count
fields.text: Required if endDate is not passed. If both are passed, count is used. Number of times to repeat the meeting pattern.

fields.name: daysOfWeek
fields.text: Required if the recurringPattern.repeats parameter is set to weekly. Days of the week that the reservable is needed.Valid values: - 1 = Monday - 2 = Tuesday - 3 = Wednesday - 4 = Thursday - 5 = Friday - 6 = Saturday - 7 = Sunday For example, to specify…

fields.name: endDate
fields.text: Required if recurringPattern.options.count is not passed. If both are passed, count is used. End date and time of the recurrence of the meeting, such as "2022-07-08T14:00:00Z".

fields.name: repeats
fields.text: Repeating pattern for the reservable.Valid values (case-sensitive): - daily - monthly - weekly - yearly

fields.name: startDate
fields.text: Start date and time for the recurring pattern, such as "2022-07-08T14:00:00Z".

params.name: reservableIds
params.text: List of sys_ids of the reservables to include in the availability score.

params.name: reservableType
params.text: Type of reservable to include in the availability score. Used to refine the search.Valid values (case-sensitive): - configuration_item - location

params.name: startEndDateTimes
params.text: List of start and end dates and times in the user's timezone to search on.Data type: Array of Objects "startEndDateTimes": [ { "end": "String", "start": "String" } ] Default: Must specify recurringPattern parameter.

fields.name: end
fields.text: End date and time of the reservable.

fields.name: start
fields.text: Start date and time of the reservable.

name: wsd-shift
title: WSD Shift API
text: The Workplace Service Delivery (WSD) Shift API provides an endpoint that returns shift time spans for a specified date and time.Returns the shift time span for a specified date/time and shift.

operations.summary: Returns the shift time span for a specified date/time and shift.

params.name: shift_id
params.text: Sys_id of the shift to retrieve the time span for.For additional information on shift-based reservations, see Enable shift-based reservation.

params.name: attempt_earlier_start
params.text: Flag that indicates whether to set an early start time if the specified start value is within the shift's time span.Valid values: - true: If the specified shift includes the date/time specified in the start parameter, return the specified start date/time as…

params.name: start
params.text: Date and time of the start of the shift time spans to return.Format: UTC - yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm:ssZ, such as 2022-05-23T08:00:00Z

params.name: timezone
params.text: Time zone to use when qualifying the shift time spans, such as ECT or PST. Also returns the shift time spans in this time zone.Format: UTC

name: wsd-unified-search
title: WSD Unified Search API
text: The WSD Unified Search API provides an endpoint to search across workplace users and locations.Searches for users and workplace locations matching the provided search term.

operations.summary: Searches for users and workplace locations matching the provided search term. Returns a combined list of matching results with pagination support.

params.name: search_term
params.text: Search query used to find matching users and workplace locations. Accepts a comma-separated list of values to search for multiple terms simultaneously. For example, "Conference, Desk" returns results matching either term. Empty segments are ignored.

params.name: show_location
params.text: Flag that indicates whether to include the user's current location in the result label.Possible values: - true: Display the user's current location in the result label. - false: Don't display the user's current location in the result label.

params.name: show_loggedin_user
params.text: Flag that indicates whether to display the authenticated user as the first result when no search term is provided. Only applies to desktop clients at offset 0. Possible values: - true: Show the authenticated user as the first result.

params.name: include_user_email
params.text: Flag that indicates whether to include user email addresses in result labels and allow searching by email address. Possible values: - true: Include email in result labels and enable email search.

params.name: filterConfig
params.text: Object containing one or more table names as keys to restrict results to specific entity types.

fields.name: <table_name>
fields.text: Flag that indicates whether to include results from the specified table. Set to true to include results from that entity type.Valid values: - true: Include results from that entity type. - false: Don't include results from that entity type.

params.name: options
params.text: Object containing additional configuration for search behavior.

fields.name: search_in_parent
fields.text: Flag that indicates whether to include results from parent location records when filtering by a child entity.Possible values: - true: Include parent location results. - false: Don't include parent location results.

fields.name: cache
fields.text: Flag that indicates whether to use cached search results.Possible values: - true: Use cached results where available. - false: Always fetch fresh results

fields.name: rsvModule
fields.text: Object containing reservation module configuration for filtering results by reservable module context.

fields.name: value
fields.text: Sys_id of the reservable module to use for filtering available spaces.

fields.name: enable_restricted_neighborhood_rules
fields.text: Flag that indicates whether to apply restricted neighborhood rules when filtering results by reservation module.Possible values: - true: Apply restricted neighborhood rules. - false: Don't apply restricted neighborhood rules.

params.name: sysparam_offset
params.text: Pagination offset. Number of records to skip before returning results. Use with sysparam_limit for pagination. Minimum value: 0

params.name: sysparam_limit
params.text: Maximum number of records to return per request. Use with sysparam_offset for pagination.Minimum value: 1

params.name: Header
params.text: Description

params.name: Accept
params.text: Data format of the response body. Supported types: application/json, application/xml, text/xml.

params.name: Content-Type
params.text: Data format of the request body: application/json.

params.name: Authorization
params.text: Authentication credentials. Supports Basic authentication or session-based authentication.

params.text: Value to include related data in the response. Uses strict equality matching (not comma-separated parsing).Note: include is only effective when the Workplace Service Delivery Concierge (com.sn_wsd_concierge) plugin is active.

params.name: past_reservations_months

params.name: future_reservations_months
